story.en: The pagoda leaves Danlugan ni Ina, passes the Panganiban, Colgante and Magsaysay bridges and approaches Dagsaan, the landing near the Basilica. Both banks and decks are crowded. The annual 16:00–18:00 replay, 120 follower boats and 16 escorts are illustrative. The 2024 gathering drew about 1.5 million devotees; the documented 2026 adjustment instead departed at 21:00 because of river conditions.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: fluvial route advisory
sources.note: Cathedral to Danlugan ni Ina, the river and the Basilica. River geometry comes from OSM; the rendered flotilla and spectators are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: updated 2026 fluvial schedule
sources.note: River conditions moved the 2026 departure to 21:00 with an estimated ninety minutes on the water. This annual replay instead uses an illustrative 16:00–18:00 window.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2024 fluvial gathering
sources.note: Reports 1.5 million devotees and the concluding Pontifical Mass at the Basilica. The crowd layout and ninety-minute Mass duration are illustrative.

sources.title: Naga Ordinance 582, section 2(23)
sources.note: Connects Santonja Street to Colgante Bridge. Matching this location to OSM way 23540251 is a geographic inference.

sources.title: Dennis T. Marpuri: Colgante eyewitness account
sources.note: January 2026 account associates former Colgante Street with present Santoja Street; corroborates the mapped bridge alias.

sources.title: Naga Tourism: 2026 Dagsaan landing
sources.note: September 20, 2026 account places the landing at Dagsaan near the Basilica, with about 1.2 million spectators. Dated night schedule is separate from this illustrative afternoon replay.
